beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: Split screen showing two diverging neural paths drifting apart in a vector space.

beats.text: Why? Because LLMs generate code one single token at a time—like a world-class chef who stops to ask you for salt before chopping every onion.
beats.visual_focus: Two bridge segments failing to connect, one jagged and low-res, the other smooth and high-res.

beats.text: Enter TRACE: it forces the training path to mirror the rollout's FP4 rounding decisions, locking them into a single, unified precision state.
beats.visual_focus: A magnetic force pulling the two drifting paths into perfect alignment.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook is killer—calling out the 'bleeding compute' issue immediately caught my attention because I've dealt with training bottlenecks before. I liked the bridge analogy; it wasn't patronizing like those 'smart drawer' videos. I got lost for a second on the technical implementation in Beat 4—I know what a mantissa is, but I'm not 100% sure how you're caching it without blowing up the cache latency. Still, it sounds like a legit optimization rather than marketing fluff.
